about: QA-144 (B79, P-319; BK-10, P-448, P-452: data, never code): what IRCC's own words set on a combination's form lines when the configured checkpoint sets it up from its forms (api/src/features/checkpoint/) and when the packs take the people's steps (acceptance/lib/pack2.ts). Read by api/src/form-setup.ts into FORM_SETUP, which names no combination and no form: a combination's form rules change here alone. Top level: 'familyFormByChannel', the family information form a combination's application form's channel picks (paper or PDF upload, online) and the one taken off; 'ruleFacts', the facts only a rule reads that more than one combination uses, each named by its key from a combination. Per combination: the application form; each form line's rule, cited with page, quote and date (P-170); the facts only a rule reads (a key from 'ruleFacts', or the fact given whole); a family information form picked by the application form's channel only when 'familyByChannel' (why each person 18 or older fills it) is given (a permanent residence application names its own family form in its rules); where its document lines come from ('documentsFromChecklist', 'documentsFromReviewedRelease' with 'documentSources', or 'documentsCited'). Status: Sample, Unconfirmed: expert (AGENTS rule 4).

familyFormByChannel.about: QA-144 slice 1 (tech lead, 4 Nov; the RCIC walk #782, IRCC-P2-04a): the family information form follows how the combination files. Each person 18 or older fills it (QA-221, ruling C: each family form keeps "each applicant, from 18", in its own words first). Sample, Unconfirmed: expert.

ruleFacts.about: QA-144 slice 3: IMM 5646's rule reads a fact no form asks (no age is worked out in this workspace), added through C3.6's door for its rule and asked of each person beside their date of birth.
